_comment: Rule-activation ratchet baseline (road-to-mixed-trigger-activation-cost step 4.1). Two axes: the scoped/mixed ID SETS are pinned by identity, and the unconditional token total may only walk DOWN. Raising a number here to clear a failing check is the config-weakening move this repo blocks by construction — every raise needs a baseline_history entry whose reason is a real sentence. Regenerate with `check_rule_activation_census --write-baseline`; never hand-edit the counts.

baseline_history.reason: Re-anchored WITH an authorized change, not to clear a red. road-to-single-delivery Phase 5.1: the four package-only rules that carried `paths:` -- no-roadmap-references, rule-type-governance, skill-quality, source-confidentiality -- had their path triggers REMOVED, so the emitter now writes no `paths:` and all four load unconditionally. Scoped 8 -> 4; unconditional corpus 108130 -> the value above, a RISE of 2882 exact-BPE tokens. The rise is the point, not a regression: ADR-236 partitions the two delivery layers, which removes each rule's unscoped global twin, and ADR-227:79-80 records that a path-scoped rule is not re-injected after `/compact` -- so leaving them scoped would let four obligations, three of them Iron Laws, vanish mid-session with nothing left to reload them. AI council 2026-08-20, 2/2 convergent (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, two rounds, blind peer review) on this option over keeping the scope, keeping an unscoped global copy, and splitting the four by CI-gate coverage. Two independent decisive arguments: the obligations govern AUTHORING decisions, which happen before any file exists for a path trigger to match (so path-scoping fails at greenfield creation, compaction aside), and rule-type-governance has NO deterministic gate at all, so for that one there is no compensating control whatsoever. Cost in context: the same change removes 96584 tokens of doubled standing prose per session (210485 -> 113901 received, overlap 113 rules / 93411 tokens -> 0), so this +2882 is 3.0 % of what the partition returns. The figure moved twice and both moves are recorded rather than smoothed: an early revision claimed 1754 tokens from a chars/4 proxy, which understated the true BPE cost by about half (measured +3512); collapsing four duplicated rationale sections into one brought it to +3156; and check_rule_stub_ceiling then refused the three short pointers outright -- a migrated stub is held at its pointer's size, so prose added there is prose in the wrong place by that gate's contract. Removing those three notes landed the final +2882, with the single shared record living in source-confidentiality, which is not a migrated stub and has no ceiling.

Re-anchored WITH the authorized change, not to clear a red. road-to-mixed-trigger-activation-cost Phase 2, amendment option (b) narrowed to the two path-dominant per-edit rules: `design-review-after-ui-write` and `ui-audit-gate` had their `component` and `design token` keyword triggers removed as an authoring decision, so the emitter restores `paths:` for both. Scoped 6 -> 8, mixed 19 -> 17, unconditional corpus 107194 -> the value above. The direction is DOWN on the weight axis and the identity move is the authorized one; the maintainer asked for this entry in the same commit so the ratchet documents its own sanctioned change instead of reporting it as drift.

Re-anchored WITH an authorized addition, not to clear a red: the new `recurring-criticism` rule plus the reconciling edits to `self-repair-loop` and `decision-revisit-gate`. The cost is structural, not sloppy authoring — the rule fires on a recurrence phrase in the USER PROMPT, and on Claude the emitter writes no `paths:` at all once any non-path trigger is present, so a prompt-triggered rule is unconditional by construction. There is no scoped variant of this obligation to choose instead: a path-scoped version would never see the prompt that triggers it, which is the whole mechanism. The body was already cut once for this reason (~45 percent, depth moved to guideline:agent-infra/recurring-criticism-mechanics, which is read on demand and costs nothing at session start); what remains is the Iron Law, the three-outcome table that is the anti-sycophancy guard, and the honest-enforcement paragraph. Trimming further would remove the reasoning the rule itself marks as the clause most likely to be trimmed. Delta 3575 tokens against a 2000 allowance, standing cost per session, stated rather than hidden.

Raised 103,265 -> 106,386 (+3,121) for one new rule, fix-what-you-see, added on maintainer instruction after a session identified a red check's cause, named the file's author, and handed it back unfixed. The rule permits exactly two dispositions -- fix it, or ship a tracked follow-up roadmap in the same change -- and removes ownership and note-only as escapes from active-remediation's ladder. WHAT THIS RE-ANCHOR EXPOSES, and it is the reason the entry is this long: the rule ships type auto rather than always because check_always_budget has two characters of headroom and its cap may only move down. That switch cleared the always gate and did NOT reduce the cost, because this census counts a rule as standing payload unless it is path-SCOPED, and a red CI check has no file pattern to scope on. So the two gates disagree about what a keyword-triggered rule costs, and the auto downgrade moved the same 3,121 tokens from a budget that refuses them into one that only asks for a sentence. Stated rather than exploited: the honest reading is that this rule costs standing payload whatever its type says, and the always-vs-auto choice bought delivery breadth, not weight.

Re-anchored for one new rule, playbook-precedence, which ships with ADR-244's sixth context type and states that a repository's OWN configured playbook outranks a shipped skill for the same task. WHY THE DELTA IS THIS LARGE, stated rather than implied: the rule is 4,398 chars of source, but it declares seven triggers and every one of them is a keyword or phrase, so the emitter writes NO `paths:` block at all and the host loads it in every session -- the same mixed-trigger cost `ui-audit-gate` and `design-review-after-ui-write` each paid before being re-scoped to paths in road-to-mixed-trigger-activation-cost Phase 2. That is the honest reading of this number: it is not the price of the obligation, it is the price of expressing the obligation with keywords. A playbook lives at a known location, so a path-scoped form is available and would return most of these tokens; it is not cut here because the trigger set is the rule author's design decision and re-cutting it inside a merge-queue drain would change routing behaviour nobody reviewed. Recorded as the next candidate for that Phase-2 treatment rather than silently absorbed.
